liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer loves the China>Rider jam, describing it as remarkable and spine-tingling [25]
- **Mountain Jam** (1 review): Review calls the performance awesome, noting all musicians participated [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-07-28.150454.SBD-AUD.composite.t-flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 32 songs; 281 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1973-07-28.135585.aud.cooper.berger.flac16**: audience recording; 31 songs; 271 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1973-07-28.sbd.weiner.181.shnf**: soundboard; 28 songs; 234 min; rated 4.27/5 by 11 [4]
- **gd73-07-28.sbd.weiner.14196.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 27 songs; 235 min; rated 4.11/5 by 56 [5]. Said about its sound: The reviewer describes the sound quality of the recording as good [16]
- **gd73-07-28.siniawsky-smith.weiner-gdADT11.11474.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 188 min; rated 3.5/5 by 6 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the source doesn't sound half bad but is on the fence; Audio quality is mediocre, sounding like it was taped on a cheap deck [23][24]
- **gd1973-07-28.152004.SonyStereo.ECM.Moskal.t.flac24**: source not stated; 24 songs; 176 min [9]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Sam Cutler [1]
- Encore features the Allman Brothers Band and The Band joining in [16]
- Robert Santelli notes approximately 600,000 people attended the Watkins Glen event [17]
- Attendees faced mud and empty water jugs, walking miles to the site [19]
- Listener walked to the site at 2 AM, settling 150 yards from stage [20]
- Arrived from Montreal, walked five miles, and woke to Jerry's guitar [21]
- Crowd of 600,000 made the day an endurance test for band and fans [26]
- Summer Jam finale included members from The Band, Allman Brothers, and Dead [1]
- Bill order: Grateful Dead opened, then The Band, then Allman Brothers [2]
- China>Rider ranks with the May 26, 1973 Ketzer China>UJBlike jam [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-07-28.150454.SBD-AUD.composite.t-flac16**: source: Soundboard Aud Composite [1]. Also: Source one supplies both sets and the unmodified encore [1]
- **gd1973-07-28.135585.aud.cooper.berger.flac16**: taped by Jim Cooper; transferred by Rob Berger; source: source: aud cassette master; taped by Jim Cooper; sony ecm22p’s > hitachi trq-232; [2]. Also: Recording patched from Jerry Moore’s master tape [2]
- **gd1973-07-28.sbd.weiner.181.shnf**: transferred by Noah Weiner; source: Soundboard [4]. Also: Analog seeds from the 1998 tree were transferred to DAT recently [4]
- **gd73-07-28.sbd.weiner.14196.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard with audience patches [5]. Also: Reviewer previously owned a fourth-generation boot of the famous soundcheck jam [27]
- **gd73-07-28.siniawsky-smith.weiner-gdADT11.11474.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jeffrey Siniawsky, Joel Smith; source: Audience Recording: Uher mic [8]
- **gd1973-07-28.152004.SonyStereo.ECM.Moskal.t.flac24**: taped by Gerry Moskal *; transferred by Gerry Moskal & Brian Mandel; source: Sony Stereo ECM ->SONY TCD126 Location: ** [9]. Also: Gerry taped on a TC-126 with a 2-point stereo microphone; Masters transferred from Gerry's reels in the mid-1980s [9]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Grand Prix Racecourse - July 28, 1973](https://www.dead.net/show/july-28-1973) [29]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Grand Prix Racecourse - July 28, 1973](https://www.dead.net/show/july-28-1973) [30]
